Jules: flagging Specter-v1 PTQ/int8 canary - structured-output funcall parse failures up. sample=1200, fails=92 (7.7%) vs fp16 mirror 4 (0.33%). saving two minimal repros.

Ivy: paste?

Jules: example1: arguments emitted as string-of-json: "arguments": "{\"id\":7,\"items\":[\"x\"]}". example2: truncated suffix on stream tail: last token is a comma not a closing brace.

Marco: pattern = double-escaped JSON OR cut-off suffix when kvcache/prefix large. int8 avg token_len +9% vs fp16 -> more cutoff risk.

Ivy: quick mitigations: (1) canary-only rescue parser: if args is string try JSON.parse(inner) then cheap sanitizers (strip trailing commas, escape raw newlines). attach telemetry original_text + rescue_applied flag. (2) one mirrored fp16 retry if rescue fails, no more retries. (3) add 200 small goldens for nested arrays to canary.

Jules: +1. ensure repair steps are logged and we don't silently mutate semantics. also limit rescue token budget.

eval-bot: eval-bot: queued micro-bench job Specter-v1 int8 vs fp16 structured-output 1k prompts (metrics: parse_fail, token_count, cutoff_count, latency).

ops-bot: ops-bot: created INF-2026-200 Specter-v1 int8 funcall parse regression (assignees: eng-ml + runtime).

Marco: I'll land a tiny harness fuzzer for double-escaped and NDJSON blank-line cases and run the bench tonight. If post-rescue fail >1% we pin to fp16 and block rollout.

Ivy: I'll open a small PR for lib/parse/rescue with tests for double-escaped, trailing-commas, truncated-suffix heuristics. tagging @Marco for review.
